results.answer: Here are the steps to troubleshoot VPN authentication failed from home, based on our runbook: **VPN authentication failed** usually means one of these: 1. **Internet check** – Open a public website (e.g., google.com) without the VPN to confirm your home internet works. 2. **Time & date** – Make sure your laptop’s clock is correct; a wrong clock breaks the VPN certificate check. 3. **Restart VPN client** – Fully quit the VPN app, reopen it, and sign in with your company email. 4. **Password expired?** – If it still says “authentication failed,” your password may have expired. Use the self-service reset page (“Forgot password” on the login screen); it sends a code to your registered phone. New passwords must be 12+ characters and not reuse your last 5 passwords. 5. **Try another network** – Connect via a phone hotspot. If it works there, your home router is likely blocking the VPN port. **If none of the above works**, open a ticket (category: network, priority: medium; high if you cannot work at all). Let me know which step you’re on or if you need the password-reset link.

This is a common one-way audio issue over VPN. Try these steps from our VoIP guide: 1) Make sure your headset is plugged in and selected as the microphone in the softphone settings. 2) Test with an internal call to another extension — if that works, the issue is with the outside line. 3) One-way audio over VPN is usually a NAT problem: disconnect the VPN, restart the softphone, then test again. 4) If you're on a desk phone, unplug the network cable for 10 seconds so it re-registers with the PBX. Let me know if internal calls work or if the issue persists after reconnecting VPN.
